svg.text: MySQL has three answers at once — and the vendor never absorbed the community one
The richest topology surface is community; the vendor API stayed deliberately small. Both ship the same one fault verb.
dbdeployer — community
downloads get TARBALL
unpack TARBALL => $HOME/opt/mysql
deploy single 8.0.4
named topologies — the only tool here with them
--topology=master-slave | group
| all-masters | fan-in
per-node scripts: start · stop · restart · kill
plus wipe_and_restart and _all variants
binaries by version dir; a build tree is
reachable via /path/to/version but undocumented
MySQL Shell AdminAPI — vendor
dba.deploySandboxInstance(3310)
dba.startSandboxInstance()
dba.stopSandboxInstance() ← graceful
dba.killSandboxInstance() ← abrupt
one instance per call, addressed by port
$HOME/mysql-sandboxes/PORT
no topology concept at the sandbox layer —
InnoDB Cluster assembly is a separate step
documented as for testing, not production
kill vs stop is a first-class distinction
mysql-test-run.pl — in-tree harness
starts servers and topologies for tests,
the MySQL analogue of PostgreSQL's Cluster.pm
absent from all three: a network partition
every answer isolates with processes and
ports, so severing a link is not expressible
the cost of sharing one host network:
dbdeployer accumulated port catalogs,
collision prevention, free-port discovery.
Containers remove the category (01-02 §4 I3).
Implication for CUBRID (01-02 §4 I2): the kill/stop split is cheap and universal — and in CUBRID it is not cosmetic.
A graceful stop runs the serial cache write-back (serial_flush_cache_pool); a crash does not. Two verbs give the most valuable scenario split for free.
Sources: dbdeployer docs/features.md + wiki/main-operations · MySQL Shell 8.0 §6.8.1–6.8.2
